title: Honest Intervals for Grid-Selected Restricted Mean Survival Time Effects at Adjacent Horizon Ties
banked_reason: D-0.5 v5 REVISE after source audit: accepted-version novelty comparison remains uninspectable; one-round operator cap exhausted before proof.
gap_reasons: The central novelty judgment remains incomplete because the closest current result, Sun2026, is an accepted article whose theorem text, assumptions, target centering, and treatment of ties could not be inspected from the accessible publisher page.

Obtain an inspectable Sun2026 accepted-manuscript PDF and map its exact grid target, penalty convention, mesh conditions, and any tie treatment against thm:phase-diameter, thm:mesh-law, and thm:phase-projection.
proof_attempt_summary: Five D-0.5 proposal versions pursued adjacent-grid-tie honest inference for adaptive RMST. The final review assigned field publishability and found no soundness or structure flags, but still required the paywalled accepted-version theorem text after a page-located arXiv v1 audit and a Zhao 2016 primary-text audit. The operator's single allowed continuation was exhausted before D0 or any Lean proof; future work needs new accepted-version evidence or a materially different source comparison, plus certification of the local hazard pair and KM/Greenwood expansions.
tldr: At an adjacent tie between population-optimal grid horizons, what interval for the grid-selected RMST effect remains honest when neighboring targets cannot be distinguished from censored trial data? The proposed phase-local result combines a smooth-hazard two-law order-\(\Delta_n\) diameter lower bound with a score-tilt projection interval having phase-uniform coverage and \(O_{P,\mathcal U}(\Delta_n+n^{-1/2})\) diameter. A joint mesh law supports these claims; certifying the hazard pair, uniform KM/Greenwood remainders, computable tolerance, and useful finite-sample length is the central work.
gap: The inspected Sun2025 arXiv:2501.15284v1 PDF p. 11 Theorem 2 assumes a unique population grid winner through \(3^{\prime\prime}\); PDF p. 12 Proposition 6 imposes that condition for each n, uses near-equispaced cells and \(m_n=k n^\gamma\), \(\gamma<1/4\). Exact adjacent ties are excluded, and the source supplies neither a tie-local observed-data diameter bound nor a phase-uniform interval for the population-grid effect. Its per-n uniqueness does not by itself rule out near-ties. The accepted article may differ.
fill: Certify the smooth two-law tie experiment and its honest-interval diameter bound; establish phase-uniform coverage and matching \(O(\Delta_n+n^{-1/2})\) diameter for a computable score-tilt projection interval on a fixed-constant trial class. Derive the mesh law and KM/Greenwood remainders needed for those claims, then compare length with a simultaneous-band fallback.
